direction: D12: Measuring cross-domain transfer without a validation set
title: Measure transfer by re-running parent and child on the real test sets in the same session; v3's generated forward panels are saturated and cannot act as a guard
verdict_cn:
可行性：中等。
一、第三版实验（v3）设计了"规则能否迁移到相似基准"的检查，但一次也没运行：49条规则有47条被标为只用于本基准，唯一一条"相似"规则提前被淘汰。即使运行，它从维基百科取材料的代码在并发时48次请求有38次被限流，18个题组有17个为空。
二、自动生成的检查题太简单：仿OfficeQA（政府财政表格问答）和仿LiveMath（数学选择题）的33道生成题，好指令、无指令、加规则三种写法共122次全部答对；故意写的"答案取整"有害文字在生成题上全对，在真实训练题上却做错4题、只多对1题（差异尚不显著）。所以生成题只能查格式，证明不了迁移。
三、同一段文字、同样60道题，不同时段通过率从50.8%掉到26.7%（服务端漂移），现行读数拿不同时段的测试分相减，会被漂移淹没。建议在同一时段交错重跑旧技能和新技能的真实测试集（每题2次），并加对照：同一规则只放本基准、无关的安慰剂文字、好指令基线；估计能分辨约2分的差别。
四、不要拿下一个基准的训练题来筛规则，那等于引入验证集。
五、最小改动：每条通过自检的规则都做"只记录、不影响决定"的影子检查，维基访问加限速重试，迁移说明栏写错不再作废整份回复；按v3记录，8个可检查步骤中有7个会运行。
what_i_did:
Read the coevo5 code: forward.py, research.py, protocol.py, step.py, gate.py, stats.py, readout.py, evaluation.py, analyst.py, skill.py, cells.py and continual_eval/backends.py. By md5 they are byte-identical in the local repo, /data/skillopt-work and the frozen v3 snapshot. Read registration v6 (sections 2.2, 5.1-5.9, 8, 12.8 and others), the v2/v3 deltas, the cal-1 registration, coevo5_transfer_sim.py and the v1 report.

Training-side measurements:
- Flattened 14,178 v3 training-side cells. The selftest unit was skipped because its name contains "test". From these I measured per-cell costs, the I-ds vs E-ds instruction effects, same-text drift between sessions, within-session flip rates, and C4' pass rates of real rule arms.
- Re-ran the earlier explorer's v3_funnel.py and smoke_forward.py; both gave byte-identical outputs.
- Extracted 8,800 cal-1 cells (old machine, read-only) and ran a resampling power study per panel size and decision rule.
- Computed T_sim standard errors analytically from the measured components.

Literature: checked the transfer protocols of GEM, TRACE, ExpeL, AWM, OPRO, MetaSPO, GEPA, ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet, Miller 2024, GSM-Symbolic and DyVal against the papers themselves (arXiv HTML/PDF).

Paid pilots on the new machine, using the frozen v3 code, routes and solver settings:
- Generation: gen1 unthrottled; gen2 throttled and stopped early; gen3 with three rule-independent target-level panels.
- Solving with the frozen deepseek solver:
  - 23 generated OfficeQA-style items with parent, scaffold and rule arms.
  - Positive controls: a decimal-hurting text, a format-breaking text and a placebo.
  - 10 generated LiveMath-style items.
- A real-item contrast on the 74-item OfficeQA training pool (parent vs the decimal-hurting text).

Wrote the full report and the Chinese verdict. No test or holdout pool was opened, and nothing was written into the repository or any run directory.
evidence:
MEASURED

v3 funnel:
- 49 proposals: 47 local, 1 invalid row, 1 similar (E-ds s3-r5, which died at support with trigger 2<4). 0 forward panels in 10 chain-steps.
- v1: 3 similar proposals, 0 forward panels.
- 2 of 13 analyst replies were voided only because the transfer-slot reason was over 300 characters (307 and 321). Each re-ask cost about 60-82k tokens.

Forward generation:
- The v3 Wikipedia client got HTTP 429 on 38 of 48 requests at 6 threads.
- gen1 (frozen code, 6 parallel): 17 of 18 panels empty, 89/90 material requests found nothing, 105,667 GLM tokens.
- gen3 (throttled, with retries): 3 of 3 panels short (7, 3, 7 valid items; minimum is 8). 53 HTTP-429 retries over 117 requests. 111,728 GLM tokens, about 6.6k per valid item.
- Across 6 sequential or throttled builds, 2 reached 8 items.
- One page supplied 3-4 of 5 rounds per panel. One near-duplicate (same formula) slipped past text deduplication.

Do generated panels discriminate?
- 23 generated OfficeQA-style items: parent 46/46, scaffold 23/23, rule-at-similar-placement 23/23.
- Decimal-hurting text H1: 23/23. Placebo: 23/23. Numbers-in-words text H2: 3/23.
- 10 generated LiveMath-style items: parent 20/20, scaffold 10/10.
- Real OfficeQA training pool, parent vs H1 (130 of 148 cells; 57 paired items): H1 lost 4 items and gained 1, -5.3 points [-12.3, +1.8], sign test p=0.375, not significant. All 4 lost items have decimal answers.
- 65% of real OfficeQA items (48 of 74) are failed under both texts; for LiveMath, 50 of 100.

Drift between sessions (same text hash ee9b737f16b8, same 60 OfficeQA items, 120 cells per session): 50.8%, 26.7%, 26.7%, 34.2% pass. Standard deviation of session means: 11.4 points for I-ds OfficeQA, 1.3 for E-ds.

Within-session flip rates: OfficeQA 0.125/0.067, LiveMath 0.162/0.128, SearchQA 0.033/0.042 (I-ds/E-ds).

cal-1 resampling (SearchQA, one session, candidate 1 run / parent 2 runs):

| Panel size | Neutral text passes C4' (1 round/2 rounds) | -10-point text passes | -3.8-point text passes | +9.1-point effect detected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| n=12 | 0.66/0.43 | 0.25/0.09 | 0.44/0.23 | 0.17 |
| n=60 | 0.61/0.35 | 0.03/0.00 | 0.20/0.05 | 0.63 |
| n=100 | — | — | — | 0.83 |

A +3.4-point effect needs more than 400 items (power 0.73 at n=400).

Instruction effect, I-ds vs E-ds on v3 training items: SearchQA +3.2 [-0.2, 7.0], OfficeQA +4.7 [-1.4, 11.5], LiveMath -4.5 [-10, 1], ALFWorld +10.5 [2.6, 18.4]. Only ALFWorld is significant.

ESTIMATED: T_sim standard error is 5.79 points with the registered readout and measured I-ds drift (1.06 with no drift), versus 0.84 with paired same-session evaluation at 2 runs per arm. That puts the detectable effect at about 14 points vs about 2.

CLAIM: none of the 12 papers uses generated similar-target items as transfer evidence. All of them measure on the target's held-out test set against a baseline that did not learn.
design:
1) Split the three jobs that v3 gives one forward panel.
- A. Selection guard (C4'): blocks visible harm only and is never evidence.
- B. Co-evolution signal: a generated stream with guaranteed answers that the roles may see.
- C. Measurement: sealed real test sets.

2) Measurement:
- At each step where the Skill changed, re-evaluate parent and child together on the similar targets' (and dissimilar targets') test sets, interleaved in one session, 2 runs per arm.
- Report each cell's paired difference with its CI, and T_sim as the mean of the 5 similar cells (minimum detectable effect about 2 points, estimated).
- Controls in the same session: the same rule placed only locally (separates the similar placement from local-text bleed), a length-matched placebo, and the good-instruction Skill as the baseline that did not learn (the counterpart of GEM's b).
- Keep the registered 12.8 readout only as a secondary number, labelled as exposed to drift.

3) Similar-target panels:
- Do not sample the next benchmark's training pool. It breaks registration 2.2, turns that pool into a validation set, and causes adaptive reuse later.
- Backward targets keep the real 60-item regression panels.
- Forward targets: the v3 generated panel is only a format check. Replace it with a hardened generator only if, on a frozen bank, its items reproduce the real benchmark's mix of solved and unsolved items.
- If one qualifies: one rule-independent target-level panel per target per step, about 40 items x 2 runs, drawn before the analyst replies and seeded by a hash of (run, chain, step, target). Material comes from a frozen, revision-pinned bank, fetched through a throttled client. The panel is shared by all candidates and controls, and a short panel is recorded as "unchecked".

4) Scoring: same frozen solver and native scorer, L/H bounds, arms interleaved, completion length logged to audit the serving mode.

5) Isolation:
- Separate namespaces and directories (fwd:/sig:/test) with a path guard.
- No role sees panel items or scores, only accept/reject status.
- The generator never sees the rule.
- Fresh draws every step.
- Deduplicate A against B by normalized text, formula and source revision.
- Post-run audit: hash every selection and measurement item and search all role transcripts for them.

6) Minimal v3 change: step.py line 585 becomes `similar = [i for i in supported if targets]`, run as a logged shadow C4' check that leaves the local verdict alone. Also:
- one shared panel per target;
- throttle Wikipedia with 429 retry;
- do not void the analyst reply over the transfer slot;
- raise FORWARD_PANEL together with the check at gate.py line 93.

On v3 records this would have exercised C4' at 7 of 8 checkable chain-steps, with generated panels at only 3 of them. Step 5 has no similar target.

pilot.result:
Generated forward panels are saturated for the frozen solver: 122 of 122 cells passed for the parent, scaffold and rule arms. That covers 23 OfficeQA-style items (92 cells) and 10 LiveMath-style items (30 cells). A text written to hurt decimal answers passed 23 of 23 on generated items. On the real OfficeQA training pool the same text lost 4 items and gained 1 (57 paired items; -5.3 points [-12.3, +1.8], p=0.375, not significant), and all 4 lost items have decimal answers. Only blatant format breakage registered on generated items (numbers in words: 3 of 23 passed).

Generation: unthrottled v3 code at 6 threads gave 17 of 18 empty panels because of Wikipedia HTTP 429. Throttled target-level panels were all short (7, 3, 7 valid items).

Deviations and stops, all disclosed:
- gen2 was stopped after 17 minutes for the 05:59 hand-over.
- A first solve attempt ran about 4 minutes alongside gen2, above the concurrency limit of 6. I stopped it when I noticed; it had saved no cells.
- The real-pool run was stopped at 130 of 148 cells because the shared deepseek route was rate-limiting.

Recorded tokens: 2,006,195 (GLM 217,395; deepseek 1,788,800). Not recorded: gen2 (estimated 0.2-0.4M GLM), solve1 (fewer than 20 cells) and diagnostics (about 10k). Estimated total about 2.3-2.4M, under the 3M cap.
pilot.blocked_by: Nothing was denied by the permission system. Remaining limits: the shared deepseek route rate-limited (HTTP 429 backoff up to 300 s per call) while other explorers' pilots ran, and the 05:59 hand-over.

risks:
- Construct validity: generated items are one-step arithmetic on small Wikipedia tables, or elementary number theory. The real benchmarks are long Treasury Bulletin pages and research-level theorem MCQs. A harder generator may still fail the qualification.
- Serving drift: any comparison across sessions can move 10-25 points on OfficeQA for the same text. The paired same-session design removes this, but it needs a new registration version and more test access.
- Small similar test sets: OfficeQA 172 and LiveMath 125 cannot resolve 3-point single-cell effects; only the pooled T_sim gets near 2 points.
- The pilots are small. 33 generated items, and the real-pool contrast is not significant (57 paired items). Saturation is shown for this solver and these generators only.
- The similar-pair map is declared, not measured. MetaSPO found gain correlates with measured similarity (r=0.56), so similarity per pair is worth recording.
- Shadow checks spend tokens without changing decisions; they are worth it only as measurement of the guard.
- The shared deepseek route rate-limits under concurrent pilots. Test re-evaluation at scale needs a quiet window or quota.
- The drift standard deviations rest on 3-4 sessions, so their own relative error is about 40%.
cost_estimate:
All figures are estimated from measured per-cell costs: mean total tokens per cell were SearchQA 2,353, OfficeQA 5,847 (9.4k in a verbose session), LiveMath 2,994 and generated items about 3.5k.

| Item | Tokens |
|---|---|
| Paired measurement, OfficeQA, 2 runs per arm, one changed step | about 4.0M |
| Paired measurement, LiveMath, same | about 1.5M |
| Paired measurement, SearchQA, same | about 3.8M |
| All 5 similar cells of one chain, if every step changed | about 17M (about 8.7M at 1 run) |
| Hardened 40-item selection panel, generation, per target per step | about 0.1-0.3M GLM |
| Same panel, solving, per candidate | about 0.3M |
| Shadow C4' for a v3-like funnel | 9 per-rule panels, or 3 shared |

Steps where the Skill is unchanged cost nothing (records reused). The paired re-evaluation roughly doubles the test cost of each changed step. Implementing the minimal shadow change is about 20 lines plus a protocol version; one shadow run over the v3 chains' supported rules is estimated at 1-3M tokens.
recommendation:
1. Register v5 transfer measurement as paired same-session re-evaluation of parent and child on the similar targets' test sets, 2 runs per arm, in a new version. Include the local-placement control, a placebo and the good-instruction baseline. Report T_sim with its paired CI, and keep the 12.8 readout as a labelled number exposed to drift.
2. Do not use the v3-style generated forward panel as a guard: it was saturated (122/122) and short in 4 of 6 builds. Keep it as a format check, or qualify a hardened generator first: on a frozen bank, its pass rate and the share of items where the good instruction and the scaffold disagree must match the real benchmark.
3. Never sample the next benchmark's training pool before its own step. If the owner wants a real-item forward guard anyway, that is a different claim ("transfer with target validation data") and needs an explicit decision.
4. Keep the real 60-item regression panels for backward targets.
5. To see the machinery run, implement the shadow change in step.py with a Wikipedia throttle and a non-voiding transfer slot, and replay it on the v3 supported rules (7 of 8 checkable steps).
